messages:
devon: Quick Q — if a request arrives with an expired API key but a valid `X-Project` header, should our public API return 401 (unauth) or 403 (forbidden)? Observed some clients getting 403 from older gateway paths.

anika: 401 for expired/invalid credentials. 403 should mean credentials are valid but not authorized for that project/operation.

samir: Agreed. SDKs treat 403 as a hard failure in some cases, so returning 403 on expiry causes clients not to attempt refresh. We should standardize.

josh: +1. Also recommend WWW-Authenticate header on 401 with an error code so automated clients can detect 'expired' vs 'invalid'. e.g. `WWW-Authenticate: Redwood realm=\"api\", error=\"token_expired\"`

maria: note: our edge proxy (old nginx config) sometimes strips `X-Project` when auth header is missing. That led to 400s in prod before. Need to make behaviour explicit: missing auth -> 401, present auth but expired -> 401+error, auth valid but project mismatch -> 403.

devon: SDK compatibility: currently the JS SDK maps 401->retry with refresh, 403->throw. If we switch some paths from 403->401 on expiry, it'll help clients auto-retry after refresh.

infra-bot: deploy: edge-nginx@staging rolled out at 2024-03-12T09:25:00Z. No alerts.

samir: Proposal PR: standardize responses and add short response header `X-Auth-Error: token_expired|invalid_key|insufficient_scope` for easier parsing by proxies that can't read WWW-Authenticate. Thoughts on leaking info?

josh: I like the header for telemetry/debugging, but keep values generic. Don't include project ids or user info. `token_expired` is okay.

anika: security note: exposing `token_expired` in responses is acceptable, it's the same as WWW-Authenticate semantics. We shouldn't include anything more specific. Also add a flag in telemetry so support team can filter these events.

maria: Action: update ingress config to stop stripping `X-Project` when Authorization absent, and treat order: if auth missing -> 401, else validate key -> if expired -> 401 + header, else check project permission -> 403 if mismatch.

devon: sample curl clients are hitting this; here's what I'll ask SDKs to do for now so we don't break users:

```bash
# client should treat 401 with WWW-Authenticate:error=token_expired as transient and try refresh once
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Project: proj_123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

samir: created RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/112 — includes response examples + ingress change. Please review.

josh: I'll review this afternoon. Suggest adding a test matrix for proxies + SDKs so we don't regress.

anika: I'll add unit tests for auth handler mapping and a short integration test for the ingress behavior.

devon: Great. Summary/action items: 1) change expired-key responses to 401 + WWW-Authenticate (samir to update service), 2) add `X-Auth-Error` response header (samir + security), 3) update ingress nginx to not strip X-Project (maria), 4) SDKs treat 401+token_expired as retry-with-refresh (devon/josh), 5) add tests and telemetry flags (anika).

maria: noted — will open the infra PR for nginx today and ping here when staged.

devon: thanks all :thumbsup:
